informal: The Lean models a rank channel as a uniform pair (nonzero frame vector, offset) in \(\mathbb F_P^4\), with \(y\) retained at level \(k\) when all coordinates of \(a(y)\) lie below \(\lceil P2^{-k}\rceil\), and proves the exact marginal retention probability \(\pi_{b_k}\), the conditional pair bound, and the mean and variance of retained counts.

results.informal: For the affine channel, \(\Pr\{X_{b_k}(y)=1\}=\pi_{b_k}\); for \(y\ne x\), \(\Pr\{X_{b_j}(y)=1\mid X_{b_k}(x)=1\}\le 2\pi_{b_j}\) (and \(\le\pi_{b_j}\) when \(k=j\)); and for a set \(A_0\) of \(q\) distinct identifiers, \(T=\sum_{y\in A_0}X_{b_k}(y)\) has \(\mathbb E T=q\pi_{b_k}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}T\le q\pi_{b_k}\).
results.note: These lemmas give items 1 to 3 of the paper lemma for the Lean channel (frame of one column, \(H=4\)); item 3 is stated as a variance bound rather than the Chebyshev tail, and the rate comparison \(b_k\le\pi_{b_k}\le16b_k\) is the separate lemma pct_bounds.

decls.name: marginal
decls.informal: \(\mathbb E[X_{b_k}(y)]=\pi_{b_k}\), i.e. a specified identifier \(y\) is retained at level \(k\) with probability exactly \(\pi_{b_k}\).

decls.name: pairMean
decls.informal: If \(y\ne x\) then \(\mathbb E[X_{b_j}(y)\mid X_{b_k}(x)=1]\le 2\pi_{b_j}\), and if moreover \(k=j\) then \(\mathbb E[X_{b_j}(y)\mid X_{b_k}(x)=1]\le\pi_{b_j}\).

chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/0: For a fixed retained value \(v\) of \(a(x)\) and a frame \(F\), let \(f_v(F)\) be the indicator that \(y\) is retained at level \(j\), and let \(\text{value}(v)\) be its average over frames.
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/1: The conditional expectation \(\mathbb E[X_{b_j}(y)\mid X_{b_k}(x)=1]\) equals the average of \(\text{value}(v)\) over retained values \(v\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/2: Let \(M\) be the number of frames (nonzero vectors) and \(N=P^4\) the number of all vectors.
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5: For each retained value \(v\), \(M\cdot\text{value}(v)+\mathbf 1\{v\text{ lies in the level-}j\text{ box}\}=N\pi_{b_j}\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5/0: Averaging the box indicator over \(v+(y-x)F\) for nonzero frames \(F\) and adding the value at \(v\) gives \(N\) times the box average, since \(y-x\ne0\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5/1: The average of the level-\(j\) box indicator over all vectors is \(\pi_{b_j}\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5/2: \(f_v(F)\) is the box indicator evaluated at \(v+(y-x)F\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5/2/2: Hence \(f_v(F)\) is the box indicator at \(v+(y-x)F\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/5/3: Substituting this into the averaging identity gives the claim.
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/7/0: It suffices to show \(\text{value}(v)\le2\pi_{b_j}\) for each \(v\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/8: Now assume \(k=j\); it suffices to show \(\text{value}(v)\le\pi_{b_j}\) for each \(v\).
chunks.AffineSampling.pairMean/10: When \(k=j\) the value \(v\) itself lies in the box, so the indicator is \(1\).

decls.name: count_var
decls.informal: If \(g\) is injective on \(s\) and \(T=\sum_{j\in s}X_{b_k}(g(j))\), then \(\mathbb E T=|s|\pi_{b_k}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}T\le|s|\pi_{b_k}\).

chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/1: \(\mathbb E T=|s|p\), by linearity and the exact marginal.
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/2: It remains to show \(\mathbb E T^2-(\mathbb E T)^2\le|s|p\).
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/3/1: If \(a=b\), the product is \(X_{b_k}(g(a))\), whose mean is \(p\le p^2+p\).
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/3/2: If \(a\ne b\), the bound \(p^2\) follows from the conditional pair bound.
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/3/2/0: Write the mean as \(p\cdot\mathbb E[X_{b_k}(g(b))\mid X_{b_k}(g(a))=1]\).
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/3/2/1: Since \(g(a)\ne g(b)\), the conditional mean is at most \(p\) at equal levels.
chunks.AffineSampling.count_var/5: Summing the pair bound gives \(\mathbb E T^2\le\sum_a\sum_b(p^2+\mathbf 1\{a=b\}p)\).
